title: Bakery and Promise
premise: Oscar Blackwood, a ghostwriter who hides behind other people's words, is hired to pen the memoirs of rival baker Marguerite Voss — the woman whose family bakery once crushed his own. To survive the Blackwood family reunion, he recruits Delphine, Marguerite's estranged daughter and heir apparent, as a fake date; by dessert their pretense has curdled into something real. As Oscar uncovers in Marguerite's memoirs that his father's ruin was not her doing but her silence bought by his own family, he must choose between finishing the book that will secure his career and exposing the truth that could save Delphine's inheritance — and their love. In the end, Oscar publishes the unvarnished manuscript under his own name, loses the ghostwriting world but gains the bakery's second oven, a shared name on the lease, and a promise kept out loud.
about_author: Jude Blackwood is the pen name of a former pastry line cook who traded early mornings for late nights at the keyboard. They write love stories about people who inherit more debts than treasures, set in kitchens where flour dust hangs like memory.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A ghostwriter with five years of small safe steps behind him accepts the memoir commission from Marguerite Voss, the rival baker whose name still tastes like his father's bankruptcy. He tells himself it's just work. Emotional beat: guarded ambition masking old grief.

chapters.title: The Reunion Clause
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. His mother summons him to the Blackwood reunion with a plus-one required and questions guaranteed. Panicked, he asks Delphine Voss — met once in Marguerite's doorway — to pose as his date. She agrees for reasons she won't share. Emotional beat: reckless improvisation over dread.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The fake date works too well: Delphine charms his impossible aunt, Oscar defends her against a backhanded toast, and by dessert they're holding hands without remembering when it started. Emotional beat: the terrifying warmth of something unplanned.

chapters.title: Second Oven
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Delphine returns to the bakery she fled seven years ago, now under pressure to sell the building. Watching Oscar interview her mother, she sees how gently he handles other people's stories — and how he avoids his own. Emotional beat: homesickness tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Transcribing Marguerite's tapes, Oscar finds an account of the 2019 buyout that contradicts everything his family told him: the Vosses didn't destroy his father's bakery — they were paid to stay silent about who did. Emotional beat: vertigo as the villain changes shape.

chapters.title: Lent Pieces
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Delphine discovers Oscar's identity as the son of the baker her mother ruined-by-silence, and confronts him. He admits what the memoir reveals but begs her to let him finish the book before deciding anything. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with reluctant understanding.

chapters.title: What the Contract Says
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Marguerite's lawyer threatens litigation if the buyout chapter survives editing; his career, his apartment, his five safe years hang on compliance. Meanwhile the sale of the bakery building accelerates. Emotional beat: duty closing like a fist.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the eve of the sale signing, Oscar and Delphine bake together through the night — bread instead of words — and admit they love each other, which makes every coming choice cost double. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Unvarnished Manuscript
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the memoir launch, Oscar abandons the approved text and reads the true chapter aloud, naming his own family as the buyer and Marguerite as a silenced witness. The room detonates; his career does too. Emotional beat: climax — ruin chosen freely.

chapters.title: Promise, Kept Warm
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Months later: the sale collapsed, the bakery reorganized with Delphine as heir and Marguerite finally telling her story herself. Oscar arrives with flour on his sleeves and a lease amendment bearing both names. Emotional beat: resolution — the whole heart, risked and returned.
